chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal or someone else, from Jameel, from Aban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man who bequeathed 'something' from his wealth. He said: 'The 'something' in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one-sixth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of 'something' (shay') when a person bequeaths an unspecified portion of their wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ambiguous term 'something' (shay') in bequests by anchoring it to the authoritative interpretation in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), establishing one-sixth as the standard limit. This ruling aligns with the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific textual precedents from the Imams resolve generalities in inheritance law, ensuring consistency with the Prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazaal, or someone else, from Jameel, from Aban, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who bequeathed with ‘something’ from his wealth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ‘something’ in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> is (one) from six (1/6)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal or others from Jamil from Aban who has narrated the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
was asked about the case of a man who made a will about something of his legacy. He (the Imam) said, ‘According to the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, it is one-sixth.’”
